title: Shifting of the Burden of Proof
description: Making a claim that needs justification, then demanding that the opponent justifies the opposite of the claim. The burden of proof is a legal and philosophical concept with differences in each domain. In everyday debate, the burden of proof typically lies with the person making the claim, but it can also lie with the person denying a well-established fact or theory. Like other non-black and white issues, there are instances where this is clearly fallacious, and those which are not as clear.
logical_form:
Person 1 is claiming Y, which requires justification.

Person 1 demands that person 2 justify the opposite of Y.

Person 2 refuses or is unable to comply.

Therefore, Y is true.

examples.example:
Jack: I have tiny, invisible unicorns living in my anus.

Nick: How do you figure?

Jack: Can you prove that I don't?

Nick: No.

Jack: Then I do.
examples.explanation: Jack made a claim that requires justification. Nick asked for the evidence, but Jack shifted the burden of proof to Nick. When Nick was unable to refute Jack's (*[unfalsifiable](https://www.logicallyfallacious.com/logicalfallacies/Unfalsifiability)*) claim, Jack claimed victory.

examples.example:
Audrey: I am a human being. I am not a cyborg from the future here to destroy humanity.

Fred: Prove that you are human! Cyborgs don't pass out when they lose a lot of blood. Here's a knife.

Audrey: Get to bed, Freddie. And no more SYFY channel before bed!
examples.explanation: Audrey is making a claim of common knowledge, perhaps sparked by Fred's suspicions. Fred is asking Audrey to prove the claim when he is the one that should be justifying his objection to the claim of common knowledge.

exceptions: Again, the question of who has the burden of proof is not always as simple as demonstrated in these examples. Often, this is an argument itself.
tips: If possible, justify your argument with evidence even if you might not have the burden of proof. The only time you might not want to do this is when it gives credibility to an outrageous accusation or claim.
references: Bunnin, N., & Yu, J. (2008). *The Blackwell Dictionary of Western Philosophy*. John Wiley & Sons.
description_et: Põhjendust vajava väite esitamine, seejärel nõudmine, et oponent põhjendaks väite vastupidist. Tõendamiskohustus on juriidiline ja filosoofiline kontseptsioon, millel on igas valdkonnas erinevusi. Igapäevases arutelus lasub tõendamiskoormus tavaliselt väite esitajal, kuid see võib olla ka isikul, kes eitab väljakujunenud fakti või teooriat. Sarnaselt muudele mittemust-valgetele probleemidele on juhtumeid, kus see on selgelt ekslik, ja juhtumeid, mis pole nii selged.
logical_form_et:
Isik 1 väidab Y, mis nõuab põhjendust.

Isik 1 nõuab, et isik 2 õigustaks Y vastandit.

Isik 2 keeldub või ei suuda seda täita.

Seetõttu on Y tõsi.
exceptions_et: Jällegi, küsimus, kellel on tõendamiskohustus, ei ole alati nii lihtne, nagu nendes näidetes näidatud. Sageli on see argument iseenesest.
tips_et: Võimaluse korral põhjendage oma väidet tõenditega, isegi kui teil ei pruugi olla tõendamiskohustust. Ainus kord, kui te ei pruugi seda teha, on siis, kui see annab ennekuulmatule süüdistusele või väitele usaldusväärsuse.

examples_et.example:
Jack: Minu pärakus elavad pisikesed nähtamatud ükssarved.

Nick: Kuidas sa aru saad?

Jack: Kas sa saad tõestada, et ma seda ei tee?

Nick: Ei.

Jack: Siis ma teen.
examples_et.explanation: Jack esitas väite, mis nõuab õigustust. Nick palus tõendeid, kuid Jack lükkas tõendamiskohustuse Nickile. Kui Nick ei suutnud Jacki (*[unfalsifiable](https://www.logicallyfallacious.com/logicalfallacies/Unfalsifiability)*) väidet ümber lükata, väitis Jack võidu.

Fred: Tõesta, et oled inimene! Küborgid ei minesta, kui nad kaotavad palju verd. Siin on nuga.

Audrey: Mine magama, Freddie. Ja enne magamaminekut pole enam SYFY kanalit!
